findings.title: Load one coherent committed SQLite Conversation snapshot
findings.summary: P2: SqliteConversationStore.load performs independent SELECTs without a read transaction under the tested CPython legacy transaction mode. Two real SQLite connections in WAL mode deterministically interleave a legitimate save between History and continuation reads. Public load returns History A with thread-B, a state never committed by either save; final DB is B/thread-B. This is not a claim of active native model harm: maintained non-test store consumers were not found.
findings.acceptance: A public load must return one complete committed snapshot, not cross-commit History/ref combinations. Add deterministic WAL and default-journal reader/writer regressions using independent expected pairs, including missing-record and failure/cleanup controls. Establish the read consistency boundary across all SELECTs while preserving atomic saves, schema compatibility, busy semantics and closure. Do not replace the store, add an ORM or claim power-loss/exactly-once guarantees.

findings.title: Make initial SQLite Conversation schema installation atomic
findings.summary: P2: _ensure_schema wraps executescript in a connection context but the DDL script has no explicit transaction. A deterministic SQLite authorizer denial on the second CREATE TABLE occurs after sessions is durably installed at user_version0. The connection closes; ordinary save retry refuses this self-created nonempty v0 database as PersistenceFormatError. No data was deleted and fail-closed refusal after partial state is appropriate; partial installation is the defect.
findings.acceptance: Install fresh schema tables, indexes and user_version together or roll back to the original empty state on a controlled intermediate failure. Test failures during tables/index/version setup, connection closure, clean retry and successful save/load. Preserve byte/data custody and refusal for unrelated nonempty databases or preexisting unknown partial schemas; do not auto-delete/reinitialize them. Keep supported v1 schema unchanged and avoid a migration/recovery framework.

findings.title: Reject non-text SQLite Conversation payload and continuation values
findings.summary: P2: a valid store-created v1 SQLite database permits BLOB storage classes in TEXT-affinity columns. Public load admits bytes in messages.content/source and conversations.source/value because the reconstructed dataclasses do not validate all string types. Four actual SQL updates reproduce invalid returned state; a fifth Runtime consumer probe forwards a bytes-valued continuation to its deterministic interaction. The strict JSON persistence path rejects wrong value types. No real provider or actual user database was exercised.
findings.acceptance: Validate persisted semantic text at the SQLite decoding boundary before constructing Message/InteractionSource/ConversationRef. Refuse unsupported storage classes as PersistenceFormatError with appropriate causes; do not lossy-decode/coerce bytes. Cover all four demonstrated columns, valid Unicode/empty content, existing timestamp/ID/role/ref failures, duplicate occurrences, shared message identity and Runtime restoration. Keep valid v1 wire/schema and source/identity semantics; no global Model/Conversation redesign.

known_limits: Caller-coordinated synchronous capture, not a thread/process snapshot lock
Current replacement, no compare-and-swap or historical timeline; orphan message retention
Raw SQLite operational/corruption errors remain outside PersistenceError
No universal input/resource/environment or power-loss assurance
No maintained non-test Conversation JSON/SQLite persistence caller found
consumer_search: Exact API and persistence import searches across maintained src/apps/scripts/tests plus bounded experiment code excluding frozen runs; only package internals/tests matched direct save/load/encode/decode.
